facts.statement: In May 1906, fossil trader Bernhard Hauff discovered a uniquely complete plesiosaur skeleton in a dump of discarded rocks from a quarry near Holzmaden.
facts.quote: In May 1906, the famous fossil trader Bernhard Hauff discovered in the dump broken-up boulders containing an uniquely complete and thus very rare plesiosaur skeleton.

facts.statement: It took over nine months for Bernhard Hauff to recover 2.5 tonnes of chalkstone to expose and prepare the bones of the skeleton.
facts.quote: Over nine months he recovered 2.5 tonnes of chalkstone, exposing and preparing the bones.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton was smashed to pieces during a firestorm in Stuttgart on September 12, 1944, caused by British bombers.
facts.quote: In 1944, Stuttgart was repeatedly bombed. On 12 September, British bombers caused a firestorm that burnt the inner city. The museum was destroyed and the holotype smashed to pieces.

facts.statement: Meyerasaurus lived in the early Toarcian stage of the Early Jurassic, approximately 183 to 180 million years ago, in the Posidonia Shale lagerstätte.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Harpoceras elegantulum-falciferum ammonoid subzones, Harpoceras falcifer zone, of the famous Posidonien-Schiefer lagerstätte (Posidonia Shale), dating to the early Toarcian stage of the Early Jurassic, about 183-180 million years ago.

facts.statement: The genus Meyerasaurus was first named by Adam S. Smith and Peggy Vincent in 2010, establishing the valid species name Meyerasaurus victor.
facts.quote: Meyerasaurus was first named by Adam S. Smith and Peggy Vincent in 2010 and the combinatio nova is Meyerasaurus victor.

facts.statement: The generic name Meyerasaurus honors the German paleontologist Hermann von Meyer, who originally proposed the name Thaumatosaurus.
facts.quote: The generic name honors the German palaeontologist Hermann von Meyer for proposing the generic name Thaumatosaurus.

facts.statement: The parent group of Meyerasaurus is the family Rhomaleosauridae.
Meyerasaurus lived during the Toarcian stage, between 184.2 and 182.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 182.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The reassembled holotype skeleton of Meyerasaurus is currently displayed at the Museum am Löwentor in Stuttgart.
facts.quote: It is now displayed in the new paleontology exhibition building, the Museum am Löwentor.

facts.statement: In 2007, Adam Stuart Smith proposed creating a separate genus for the taxon because he considered the original name Thaumatosaurus to be a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: In 2007, Adam Stuart Smith announced that he would shortly name a separate genus for the taxon as Thaumatosaurus was basically a nomen dubium.

rejected.quote: Meyerasaurus is an extinct genus of rhomaleosaurid plesiosaur known from the Early Jurassic of Holzmaden, Baden-Württemberg in southwestern Germany.
